title: inbox\settings.json schema 5: schema 4 (R1 tiers) with the hard VM lifetime cap (owner decision Q4) in place of lease_wall_clock_hours
x-owner: P09.x (the cap rule, allocator.md); P12.3 (supervisor reader); P20.1 (tray writer). Schema 4 stays the live contract until the supervisor lists 5 in status.v5.json settings_schemas

linux_backend.description: Supervisor-side; the tray writes back what status.v5.json reports and never changes it. Flipped only by the cutover item P27. Default wsl-legacy.

linux_light_count.description: Light tier slots (labels self-hosted,linux,x64,fresh,light): reservation 1 CPU / 3 GiB, hard cap 4 CPU / 8 GiB each (docs/ROADMAP.md R1).

linux_heavy_count.description: Heavy tier slots (labels self-hosted,linux,x64,fresh,heavy): reservation 8 CPU / 20 GiB each, may burst to the pool, 4x CPU weight.

windows_runner_count.description: 0..5; not counted against the Linux tiers.

job_cpus.description: The legacy WSL pool CPU total, as in schema 3 (the Linux per-slot limits come from the tier table, not from settings); same range as schema 3.

job_memory_gib.description: The legacy WSL pool memory total, as in schema 3. Heavy x 20 + light x 3 GiB must not exceed it (validate.py sem_settings_v4).

vm_lifetime_cap_hours.description: The hard VM lifetime cap (allocator.md, Hard VM lifetime cap): no hyperv-vm reservation lives longer than this many hours from its acquired_at, whatever the job, the guest or GitHub says. A ceiling of 6 hours, default 6: lower is allowed, higher is refused whole and never clamped. It replaces schema 4's lease_wall_clock_hours, which only flagged.
